title: Heart a factor in death of Bagnell, doctor says
article: Robert Bagnell had a pre-existing heart condition and enough cocaine in his system to kill him the day Vancouver police restrained him using a taser, a pathologist said at a coroner's inquest yesterday.

The 44-year-old man died June 23, 2004, after police were called to a Granville Street hotel following reports that a resident was behaving erratically. He died at the scene after an altercation with police.
His death has outraged his family members who have sought to find answers as to why police resorted to the controversial tasers.

Mr. Bagnell had undergone open-heart surgery and had cardiac problems at the time of the altercation, pathologist Laurel Gray testified. She said an enlarged heart with thickened ventricles contributed in large part to his death.
"Because of the stimulant drugs, the heart has to beat faster and harder. If one is a chronic cocaine user, it makes the heart even more susceptible to arrhythmia," she said.

An enlarged heart can be an indicator of chronic abuse of drugs, such as cocaine, and Dr. Gray's conclusion was that Mr. Bagnell's death was consistent with restraint-assisted cardiac arrest due to acute cocaine intoxication.

Under questioning by lawyers representing the Vancouver Police Department and Taser International Inc., the makers of the device, Dr. Gray testified that if the victim continued to struggle after the application of the taser, then the taser was unlikely to have contributed to his death.
The five-man jury has not heard yet whether Mr. Bagnell struggled.

Under cross-examination by Mr. Ward, Dr. Gray acknowledged that a different forensic pathologist could have reached a different conclusion. An autopsy alone would not have definitively revealed how Mr. Bagnell's heart stopped, she agreed.
The inquest is expected to continue for another two weeks.
